title: Hines house-band offer and return to George Lewis, 1955
summary: Doc wanted a house band and brought Watkins out to San Francisco in August 1955. After Earl Watkins replaced him he returned to Los Angeles and rejoined George Lewis at the Beverly Cabin.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well, they're still holding now. You see, Doc had wanted a house band. Well, we couldn't take it over because we had, George had too many commitments that was taken to different places at the time that Doc wanted us there. Well, naturally he just gave it up and got oil, you know? And Ed had wrote to me and told me that Doc had wanted a house band and he wanted to use me on the drums. So Doc called me up along the distance and asked me if I would take it. He said, now, it's not anything definite. He said, but if you want to take it, I said, well, you let me know right tonight and I'll send you transportation and all. So I told him, yeah, I'd take it for a few weeks, you know? And so showing up, I went on out, he sent my transportation and I went on out there. It was in 1955 in August and we opened up on Labor Day night.
And so I went on out there and I worked with him for six weeks. And so finally Doc found a drummer boy named Earl Watkins.
Yeah, well, it wasn't the same name, but his first name was different than mine.
That's all I wondered, you know? I thought maybe some mistake that you really weren't there. I didn't know if you were there with him.

Yeah, I was there with him. And so Doc gave him my money and all. And so I came on down to Los Angeles. Well, I had put Saeed in my place before I left, see? I had to ship my drums off to New Orleans. And I stopped at the Beverly Cabin the night that they was working there. So Saeed asked me if I wanted my job back. I said, Saeed, I didn't come back here to look for my job back. I said, I'm just passed through on my way home. He said, well, you know, I'm in the civil service and my wife got a letter for me and wanted me to come on back home so I can go to work. I said, well, I said, you speak to George about that. So when they got off on the next intermission, he, George, and I, we went back in the restroom. We talked things over. So I told him, yeah, I said, well, George, you satisfied? I said, I'm tickled to death. So I had to rush, get in the rush there to check my drums and come to find out there was, had done got to Louisiana. So I had to pay $40 to have him ship back to Los Angeles. And so I sold him my, my ticket half fare. See, I told him, well, give me $25 and I said, you can have the ticket. So I've been back with the band ever since then, since 1955. But they can slow it up out there and this is a slow up here. The Beverly cabin closed down.
Yeah, that's what I hear. They closed.
